How I work

Rates & Policies

How I charge, how to schedule, what to do when the weather won't cooperate, and what I need before we fly your airplane. Read this once and there will be no surprises.

Hourly rate and payment

My rate is $100 per hour. It applies to TBDconfirm: all time together, ground and flight.

Payment is due TBDwhen, e.g. end of each session. I accept TBDpayment methods.

What the rate does not include

My rate covers my instruction only. Aircraft rental, club membership and dues, examiner fees, knowledge-test fees, headsets, books and charts are separate and are paid to whoever provides them.

Flying club and independent instruction

I instruct at West Valley Flying Club at Palo Alto (PAO) and San Carlos (SQL). Club members fly with me in club aircraft and schedule through TBDthe club's scheduling system. TBDpaid directly as an independent contractor?

I am also available on an independent basis in your own aircraft — see below.

Your own aircraft and insurance

I am glad to instruct in an airplane you own or rent. Before our first flight together I need TBDinsurance requirement, e.g. named insured + waiver of subrogation. The airplane must have a current annual inspection and the other inspections required for the flying we will do, and the maintenance records should be available for me to look at.

Scheduling and availability

TBDdays and hours available

Please contact me before scheduling:

  • your first session with me;
  • a session at night, or outside my usual hours;
  • a session at an airport other than TBDbase airport;
  • anything unusual — a long cross-country, an aircraft pickup, a trip.

My schedule tends to fill up close in. Planning a week or two ahead is the surest way to get the dates and times you want, and it usually helps with aircraft availability too.

Cancellations and weather

If you need to cancel, please give me as much notice as you can by email TBDor text or phone. Appointments cancelled with less than TBDe.g. 24 hours notice, and no-shows, TBDhow they are billed.

We keep the appointment regardless of the forecast unless we agree otherwise beforehand. If the weather is not good enough to fly, the time is well spent on ground instruction, paperwork and planning — the parts of training that usually get squeezed.

Questions

Anything on this page unclear? Email me before we fly, not after the invoice.
